summary: Updates now pause trading for about five seconds instead of a minute, and a stop that exactly covers its trade no longer shows a reconciliation warning after its take profit was canceled by hand.
minor: Updates pause trade management for about five seconds: only the trading engine restarts, and each account checks in from its own address at once.
fixes: A trade whose take profit was canceled by hand no longer keeps a stale reconciliation warning after its stop is resized to cover it exactly.
A one-time fee update to an older take profit no longer waits for a periodic account check to finish.

details.title: Shorter update pause
items: The 26 October update paused trade management for 5.3 seconds, down from about a minute in 0.10.35.1 and about three and a half minutes before 0.10.35.
The web connection restarts separately and reconnects within a second; stops and take profits stay on Hyperliquid throughout.

summary: An account no longer shows as unavailable when Hyperliquid stops listing an empty balance, stops and take profits show their current state after a Chase adds to a trade, and each account now trades from its own address.
minor: Each account now sends its Hyperliquid requests from its own network address, so one account's activity never uses up another's request allowance.
fixes: An account no longer shows Account unavailable, with its Trad commands refused, after Hyperliquid stops listing a stablecoin balance that went to zero.
A stop or take profit no longer shows as pending after it has finished when a Chase entry added to its trade or its target changed.

details.title: An address per account
items: Every request, stream and rate limit of an account runs on that account's own address; public market data is shared.
If an account cannot use its address, only that account waits; the others keep trading.

details.title: Balances Hyperliquid stops listing
items: After a reconnect Hyperliquid can stop listing stablecoin balances that are empty. Trad now removes them from your account instead of keeping the old rows.

On 25 October this left two accounts showing Account unavailable from 09:35 to 13:01 UTC, and Trad commands on them would have been refused. Fills, stops, take profits and account checks kept running, and the 0.10.35 update repaired both accounts.
The balance list may keep showing a removed zero balance until the page reloads or reconnects.

details.title: Protection status after a Chase
items: When a Chase adds to a trade or the trade's protection target changes, its stop and take profit are shown again with their current state, size and orders.

summary: Many Chases at once keep up with a fast market, updates pause trading for about a minute and a half instead of three minutes, and a stop can no longer be placed twice after a move.
minor: Chase reprices go out as fast as the market moves while Hyperliquid's request allowance has room, and slow down together only as it fills, entries before closes.
Updates are shorter: accounts are trading again about a minute and a half after an update starts, down from about three minutes.
fixes: A stop you moved can no longer be placed twice when Hyperliquid's answer about it names the order it replaced.
A flatten waiting for Hyperliquid to confirm a fill no longer waits for the next five-minute account check.
A Chase reprice held back for room goes out as soon as another Chase ends or the allowance frees up.
Trad no longer asks Hyperliquid how a cancel ended for an order it already saw end, which leaves more of the allowance for your orders.

details.title: Chase pacing
items: With room in the allowance, Chases reprice with no fixed wait between reprices.
As the allowance fills, Chases share a reprice rate that falls step by step. Entry Chases slow down first, and closes always keep room to go out.
Cancels and post-only orders of one account that go out together are sent as one request.
With 20 Chases in a fast market the slowest reprices lag about 7.5 seconds, down from 50.

details.title: Shorter updates
items: Accounts start side by side when Trad restarts instead of one after another, and spread their first exchange reads so none is refused.
This update paused trading for under a minute and a half.

details.title: Stops and flattens
items: Moving a stop cancels the old order and rests a new one under the same order id. If Hyperliquid answered with the old, canceled order, Trad could place a second stop. Trad now asks again, and flags only that trade until the exchange settles it.
A stop that filled after such a move settles the move.
A flatten whose position waits for the exchange's fill confirmation reads the position again after a few checks.

summary: Closes and stops go out without waiting on anything else, reconnecting picks up where you left off, and older trades load on demand instead of with every connection.
major: A close or flatten is never held back by a busy account, a missing order book or an account check in progress.
minor: Reconnecting after a drop or a network change resumes your account where it left off instead of downloading it again.
Older closed trades, a trade's full fill list and its order history load from the server when you open them.
A banner warns 7 days before your Hyperliquid agent wallet expires, with a Renew agent button that keeps the current agent signing until the new one is approved.
fixes: A stop you canceled by hand on Hyperliquid stays flagged after Trad's own change to it was refused, and Trad never places it again on its own.
A stop you just moved or canceled no longer shows as still working because a late exchange update arrived after the change.
A take profit Trad re-placed is never placed a second time when Hyperliquid's answer about it was unclear.
A flatten no longer gets stuck when a take profit closes one of its trades before the flatten's own close goes out.
A market close on a coin you weren't watching no longer waits a second or more for its price feed.
Trade cards say why a price feed is not live, and show reconnecting instead of an error while the connection comes back.

details.title: Exits first
items: Your orders and closes go ahead of price updates on your account, and one account's activity never slows another's.
A market close no longer waits for the price feed: if no order book is on hand, Trad reads it from Hyperliquid directly.
Fills and stops are applied the moment they arrive, also while Trad is checking your account against Hyperliquid.
Chase reprices are spaced out (at most every 250 ms for entries, 150 ms for closes) so a busy Chase cannot use up the exchange allowance your exits need.
Commands sent very fast in a row are paced (20 at once, 120 a minute); closes and flattens never are.

details.title: Faster connections and history
items: After a dropped connection Trad sends only what changed while you were away.
Large updates arrive in pieces, so prices never queue behind them.
Under Closed and All, older trades load as you scroll; each opens onto its fills and orders.
The position inspector can show a coin's closed exposures.

details.title: Agent wallet expiry
items: Hyperliquid agent wallets expire. From 7 days before, the terminal and the account settings show when.
From 24 hours before the expiry Trad refuses new trades; closes keep working until the expiry itself.
Renew agent approves a replacement in your wallet; the current agent keeps signing until the switch.

details.title: Protections and closes
items: A stop or take profit you cancel by hand stays flagged with its re-arm action, also when Hyperliquid had refused Trad's own edit of it just before.
A flatten whose close could not go out yet, and whose trade a take profit then closed, ends instead of waiting forever and blocking new trades on the account.
A stop or take profit that ended on Hyperliquid stays ended in Trad, even when an older open-orders update arrives after the change.
When Hyperliquid's answer about a re-placed take profit names the order it replaced, Trad looks again instead of placing it twice.

details.title: Sign-in
items: Trad accounts are now by invitation only. A refused sign-in says why: the email was not invited, or it still needs verifying with the login provider.

summary: Trad loads and stays responsive on slow or roaming mobile connections: prices no longer wait behind your trade history, and large accounts stop stuttering.
major: Prices on your trade cards start as soon as you connect, instead of waiting for your whole trade history to download.
minor: Large accounts update smoothly: the terminal no longer freezes for a moment on every fill.
Your account snapshot is smaller: old stop and take-profit orders and fills that no screen shows are no longer sent on connect.
fixes: On a slow connection Trad no longer downloads your whole account again when a confirmation is a few seconds late.
After a connection renewal the old connection stops sending immediately, so it no longer doubles the traffic for half a minute.
Trade cards stay on screen while Trad resyncs, marked as resyncing, instead of disappearing.
More coins can be watched at once, and a busy connection retries instead of showing a permanent price error.

details.title: Prices without waiting
items: Trad remembers which coins your trade cards show and asks for their prices the moment it connects.
If a price request gets no answer within 10 seconds, Trad asks again instead of waiting forever.

details.title: Smoother large accounts
items: Updates now cost time in proportion to what changed, not to the size of your account.
Old protection orders and fills that no screen shows stay on the server; nothing you see changes.

details.title: Slow and changing connections
items: A late confirmation no longer triggers a full re-download; Trad waits while updates keep arriving.
Connection renewals no longer stream on two connections at once.
Cards stay visible and marked as resyncing during a resync; open P&L shows "resyncing" until fresh numbers arrive.
Usage reports survive network stalls instead of being dropped.

summary: A stop you canceled by hand on Hyperliquid stays flagged and is never placed again on its own, also after a take profit took the trade flat and the entry grew it again.
fixes: A stop you canceled by hand on Hyperliquid is no longer placed again when Trad's own cancel of it finds it already gone.
An order missing from Hyperliquid's open orders is flagged on its trade, also when the trade is flat, instead of being counted as Trad's own cancel.

details.title: Hand-canceled stops
items: When Trad tried to cancel a stop you had already canceled by hand, Hyperliquid answered that the order was already canceled, and Trad took the cancel as its own. After a take profit took the trade flat and the entry then grew it, the stop could be placed again.
Now the stop stays flagged with its re-arm action, and it comes back only when you re-arm it.
Found by Trad's automated testing.

summary: Trade Hyperliquid's xyz markets, such as gold, oil and the S&P 500, from the same ticket as your crypto perps, with their fees and collateral spelled out.
major: Hyperliquid's xyz markets (xyz:GOLD, xyz:SP500 and more) can be traded from the order ticket and the Order, Chase and Trailing windows.
minor: The ticket shows each market's own exchange fee and the builder fee Trad adds, and says plainly when the exchange fee alone is above your target.
fixes: Market prices, size rules and order capacity are read for xyz markets too, not only for Hyperliquid's main markets.

details.title: xyz markets in the market picker
items: The market list is grouped into Hyperliquid and xyz. Typing "gold" finds xyz:GOLD.
Markets show as Hyperliquid writes them (xyz:GOLD), with an xyz tag on trade cards, positions and orders.
Markets Trad can't open trades on yet, such as isolated-margin-only or delisted xyz markets, are greyed out with the reason. You can still close or cancel what you already have there.
xyz trades use cross margin. Leverage changes for xyz markets are always sent as cross, even when the account is set to isolated.

details.title: Fees and collateral per market
items: xyz markets charge a different exchange fee from the main markets. The ticket shows that market's taker and maker fee for your fee tier, and the builder fee Trad adds on top.
When the exchange fee alone is above your all-in target, for example xyz:GOLD's 8.0 bps taker fee against a 5.5 target, the ticket says so and Trad adds no builder fee to those fills.

In Standard account mode the xyz markets use their own USDC balance on Hyperliquid's xyz dex. Trad shows it as "USDC · xyz dex collateral", checks it for margin, and tells you when it is empty: move USDC to the xyz dex, or switch the account to Unified Account mode.

details.title: Hyperliquid reads that skipped xyz
items: The market list now comes from Trad, so it matches what Trad can trade. If that list can't be loaded, Hyperliquid's main markets are still offered.
Mid prices, size rules and order capacity are asked for with Hyperliquid's own spelling (xyz:GOLD, kPEPE), so they work for xyz markets.

summary: The market picker now waits for you to choose a market, coming back to the Trad tab is instant, and the trade view stays smooth while prices move fast.
minor: The market picker changes the ticket's market only when you choose one: click it, press Enter, or leave the field on an exact match.
fixes: Coming back to the Trad tab no longer stalls while the page catches up.
Trade cards and charts stay smooth when prices move fast.

details.title: Market picker waits for your choice
items: Typing a ticker only filters the list. The ticket keeps its current market and price until you choose.
Choose a market by clicking it, by pressing Enter on the highlighted or exactly matching one, or by leaving the field on an exact match.
While you type, the field shows "press Enter to select" and the price next to it stays on the market the ticket has selected.
The Order, Chase and Trailing windows work the same way.

details.title: Coming back to the tab
items: Trad keeps its price connection open while the tab is in the background and catches up in one step when you return, instead of replaying every price it missed.
Returning to the tab checks your accounts at most once every 30 seconds, and a check that finds nothing new changes nothing on screen.
A failed account check in the background no longer clears your accounts from the screen.
The connection renews its sign-in on time even when the browser slows down background tabs.

details.title: Smoother trade view
items: Prices and charts update up to ten times a second instead of on every trade, which roughly halves the work the page does when markets are busy.
Trade charts keep their price scale steady instead of resizing as prices tick.
Prices are formatted much faster, and trade cards no longer redraw their dates on every update.

summary: Previews, order replies and prices are fast again: Trad no longer resends every stop and take profit to your browser on each exchange update.
fixes: Previews, command replies and prices no longer arrive seconds late, or time out, on accounts with many stops and take profits.
The order ticket no longer stays on "waiting for a fresh price" while the connection is busy.

details.title: Less traffic to your browser
items: Each Hyperliquid update about an order resent every stop and take profit the account ever had, canceled ones included: about 170 KB at a time, about twice a second, and growing with every trade.
The browser applied each one before anything else, so replies and prices queued behind them. Previews took 6 to 8 seconds and many timed out.
The closes that showed timed out had still gone through, each once.
Now only stops and take profits that need your attention are sent again. Traffic to one open browser fell from about 5.5 MB to under 2 KB every 20 seconds.

summary: Typing or switching a ticker in the order ticket no longer disconnects your price feeds, and a ticker the exchange doesn't list now shows Unknown market.
fixes: Typing or switching a ticker no longer disconnects the price feeds on your trade cards.
A ticker the exchange doesn't list shows Unknown market instead of Price unavailable.

details.title: Ticker typing and price feeds
items: The order ticket asks for a price only once you have finished typing a ticker the exchange lists, not for each letter.
Switching tickers leaves the prices on your trade cards running.
Trad no longer keeps retrying a ticker the exchange refused, and it stops retrying a failing price feed after a few tries instead of trying forever.
Trade cards redraw less while a price feed is reconnecting, so the page stays responsive.

summary: Take profits and resting limit orders on Hyperliquid now pay the same all-in fee as Chase entries, and each trade card shows the fees it was actually charged.
minor: The trade card shows the fees each trade was actually charged: entry and exit, each split into the exchange fee and Trad's fee, with the total on top.
The fee figures under Risk are now marked as estimates, so they are not mistaken for the fees charged.
fixes: Take profits and resting limit orders now pay the same all-in fee as Chase entries (5.5 bps) instead of about 2.7 bps.
Stops and market orders are unchanged.

details.title: Fees follow the order's role
items: Take profits, Chase and resting limit orders use the maker rate.
Stops, market orders and limit orders that cross the book when sent use the taker rate.
Eligible existing Trad take profits with the old fee are re-placed once at the same price and size. Stops are not touched.
Take profits within 0.5% of the market keep their queue position and wait until the market is further away. Other existing orders keep their placement fee until replaced.

details.title: Actual fees on the trade card
items: Entry and exit each show the exchange fee plus Trad's fee.
The total is marked approx. when a fill arrived without a reported fee, or when a close shared with other trades had its fee split by quantity. Hover it for the reason.

summary: A problem on one trade, or an order you place on Hyperliquid yourself, no longer stops your other Trad trades. A Chase can now fill its rest at market, and the one-tap Chase close keeps going until it fills.
minor: A Chase can send its unfilled rest at market when it times out or reaches its maximum distance. Turn it on in the trade ticket, the Chase form or the Chase close form.
The one-tap Chase close on a trade card now keeps following the book until the close fills. Cancel the Chase to stop it.
An entry Chase now stops when its price reaches the trade's own stop or take profit, instead of buying into a trade that is already stopped out or past its target.
New Hyperliquid accounts start with a 0.1% entry guard and a 3% stop guard (0.5% and 10% before). Accounts you already have keep their own values.

A trade whose stop or take profit was canceled on Hyperliquid now has a Re-arm protection button. It places Trad's stop and take profit again; orders you placed on Hyperliquid yourself are not touched.
fixes: Orders you place on Hyperliquid yourself no longer block new Trad trades.
A problem on one trade now shows on that trade only, instead of flagging every trade on the coin or the whole account.
When Hyperliquid sends something Trad cannot process, Trad keeps running and flags the order or coin it concerns, with the reason.
A stop or take profit you cancel on Hyperliquid is no longer placed again automatically when the trade's size changes. The trade is flagged instead, with the reason, until you re-arm it.

details.title: Problems stay where they are
items: Only a problem with a whole coin pauses new trades on that coin. The reason shows on that coin's trades and in the account positions.
Only a problem with the whole account pauses all new trades. The account badge then says sync blocked and shows the reason.
A flagged trade or coin shows as needs attention in the account badge. New trades elsewhere work as usual.
Closing and canceling stay available while new trades are paused.

details.title: Chase rest at market
items: The rest goes at market only when the Chase times out or reaches its maximum distance. Canceling it, or an entry Chase stopping at its own stop or take profit, sends nothing.
A Chase with no maximum distance and no expiry follows the book until it fills, so the option is off for it.
While the rest waits to be sent, for example for Hyperliquid to confirm the position, the trade card shows that and why.
For a close, the rest is a market close of that trade only, never more than the trade still holds.

details.title: Re-arm protection
items: The button shows only on a flagged trade. If Trad cannot re-arm it yet, the card says why.
A stop or take profit with no live order can get a new price first. Trad refuses one that is already through the market and asks for a new price.
Sizes and levels stay as they were. Change them with Edit protection once the trade is protected again.

channel: Long and short on one coin
summary: On Hyperliquid you can now hold a Trad long and a Trad short on the same coin as separate trades, each with its own stop, take profit and close.
minor: Opening a trade against an existing Trad trade on the same coin now starts a new trade instead of being refused.
A Trailing Entry in the other direction opens its own trade and leaves the existing Trad trade open.
fixes: The trade ticket no longer says Hyperliquid stops and take profits are reduce-only. They are plain orders sized to their own trade.
A working close on Hyperliquid is now labelled Close instead of Entry in the order lists.
A Chase that cannot start now shows its reason instead of waiting forever.

details.title: Long and short trades on one coin
items: Hyperliquid holds one net position per coin. Trad keeps each trade's size, stop, take profit and P&L separately.
Each trade closes only its own size. Closing the long leaves the short open, and the reverse.
Stops and take profits are not reduce-only, so each one stays sized to its own trade.
A leftover below Hyperliquid's $10 minimum is not closed automatically while an opposite Trad trade is open. It stays visible and closes once a reduce-only close is possible again.
Flatten still closes the whole coin on the exchange, including exposure outside Trad.

details.title: Clearer order wording
items: Stop and take-profit help text now matches each exchange: reduce-only on Binance and Bybit, plain orders on Hyperliquid.
The Trailing Entry form no longer says an opposite position is reduced first.
Old screens that previewed an order as reducing or reversing another trade were removed.

summary: Includes 0.10.24. Closes and the automatic dust close never send more than a trade still holds, a lost stop edit no longer pauses the account, and Trad reloads an account's history in seconds.
minor: When Trad has to reload an account's whole history after an update, it takes seconds instead of hours.
fixes: The automatic dust close can no longer close a whole trade: it waits while the stop is being placed or is filling, and only closes leftovers worth under $20.
Every order that reduces a trade is checked against what the trade still holds right before it is sent; one that is too large waits on that trade alone, with the reason on the order.
After a close sold past flat, the next entry fills no longer count as a new position, so Trad never protects units your account doesn't hold.
A stop edit whose answer was lost no longer pauses the account after a restart, and it settles once the moved stop fills.
A trade whose stop filled in part, or whose take profit is below the exchange minimum, finishes its protection instead of staying flagged until a restart.
A Chase that finished at a reduced size no longer pauses the account when its last cancel lands.

details.title: Dust close
items: A trade whose first entry fills were below Hyperliquid's $10 minimum could be read as dust and closed in full. The dust close now waits for the stop's order and stands down when the leftover is worth $20 or more at the stop price.
The dust close also waits while a stop of the trade is filling, and is withdrawn instead of sent when a take profit already sold the leftover.

details.title: Closes sized to what the trade holds
items: On Hyperliquid neither closes nor take profits are reduce-only, so a close sized before another exit filled could sell past flat. Trad keeps that overshoot on the trade, and later entry fills offset it before they count.
If you close the overshoot by hand, Trad sees it and protects the next entry fills as usual.
A close, flatten or Chase exit larger than what its trade still holds is held before it is sent. Only that trade waits, and canceling it retires it at once.
A flatten close that no longer fits is withdrawn, and the flatten reports it.

details.title: Stop edits and restarts
items: A stop you moved whose answer from Hyperliquid was lost settles from the exchange's own reports, also when the moved stop then fills.
A restart no longer clears Trad's own pending cancel after such an edit, which had stopped every action on the account.

details.title: Faster reloads
items: Reloading the largest account's whole history took nearly three hours without finishing and now takes about 14 seconds. Normal restarts from saved state are unchanged.

summary: A round of new automated testing found and fixed rare cases where a trade could lose its stop, a close could sell more than the trade held, or an account could pause.
fixes: A trade can no longer be left without a stop or take profit when its size changed while protection was waiting to be placed, or when a stop filled during a resize.
A close is fitted to what its trade still holds: if a take profit or stop already sold part of it, the close is reduced and says so, or withdrawn, so it cannot open a position the other way.
Exit fills reported before the entry fill they sold are kept, so stops keep matching the trade's size.
A Chase stays within its risk budget when a reprice or an early fill report races the order.
A stop that vanished from Hyperliquid without Trad canceling it is flagged and left alone, never placed again on its own.
Many rare orderings of exchange reports that could pause an account or leave an order waiting forever are handled.

details.title: Stops and take profits
items: Protection waiting to be placed for an older, smaller trade size is planned again for the current size.
A stop resize is no longer sent after the stop has filled; a refused or pointless write plans the protection again.
Take profits are placed for entry fills that arrive after a stop-out.

details.title: Closes
items: A close that a take profit or stop partly beat keeps working at the reduced size and shows why; one with nothing left to close is withdrawn.
A market order already sent is left alone.

details.title: Chase risk
items: A retargeted reprice uses the current price, and a fill shown before its execution counts at the order's limit price until the execution arrives.

details.title: Fewer account pauses
items: Rare report orders around Chase cancel-replace, full closes during entry fills, dust closes and restarts no longer stop the account.
Cancels and protection writes whose outcome stays unknown no longer wait forever.

summary: Editing a stop or take profit is safer around fills and restarts: no account pause after an update, no stop larger than the trade after a refused edit, and stops end with the trade.
fixes: A stop or take-profit edit that had failed before an update no longer pauses the account when Trad restarts.
If Hyperliquid refuses an edit after a fill shrank the trade, the stop is resized to the trade instead of staying larger than the position.
A stop or take profit that fills in part before Hyperliquid confirms it is recognised as Trad's own order instead of being reconciled as a conflict.
When partial closes or a take profit take a trade flat during a take-profit edit, the stop is canceled at once instead of waiting for the next account update.

details.title: Stop and take-profit edits
items: Every update restarts Trad. A restart rolled back an already rolled-back edit a second time, which could stop the account's processing until it was repaired.
A refused edit now hands the protection back to Trad, which resizes it to the current position.
A stop whose trade went flat during a take-profit edit is canceled in the same step, so it never sits live on a flat trade.

details.title: Found by new checks
items: Stop and take-profit edits are now covered by model checking and fuzzing, which found these four cases. Each has a test that fails without its fix.

summary: Moving a take profit on Hyperliquid no longer leaves the trade without one, and the take profit this had removed was placed again with the update.
fixes: Moving a take profit on Hyperliquid places the new one after the old one is canceled, instead of leaving the trade with only its stop.
A take profit that went missing this way was placed again at its new price when this update started.

details.title: Take-profit moves
items: Since 0.10.20 Trad cancels a take profit before placing it at the new price. When the cancel ended without a fill, Trad read the gap as a lost protection and could skip the new order.
The short gap while a take profit is replaced is now expected, and the replacement is always placed, also for a take profit moved more than once.
Stops were not affected; the trade's stop stayed live throughout.

summary: Chase and take-profit changes on Hyperliquid can no longer add unseen fills on top, every fill is counted, and a finished partial close no longer blocks the next one.
fixes: On Hyperliquid, Chase reprices, your order edits and take-profit changes now cancel first and place only the remainder, so a fill that lands during the change can no longer overfill or over-close.
Fills on a repriced order are counted by their exchange trade IDs, so a trade's size always matches what actually filled.
A fill above a Chase's maximum is recorded instead of pausing the account, and the trade stays closable.
After a stop starts filling, Trad no longer re-places the take profit for the apparent remainder.
A close that stopped at its price limit no longer blocks the close buttons.

details.title: Hyperliquid order changes
items: Hyperliquid replaces an order at the requested size when it is changed, adding any fill the old order took just before. Trad now cancels, waits for the final fill, then places the rest.
Stops are unchanged: a stop cannot be partly filled while it waits, so it is still moved in one step.
A take profit is off the book for a moment while it is replaced.

details.title: Every fill counted
items: A missed fill is fetched again on the next account check instead of being skipped once newer fills arrive.
A re-sent stop or take-profit change that times out again is checked again.

summary: A tiny leftover below the exchange minimum is now closed automatically, and a close no longer waits forever on a leftover too small to protect.
fixes: When a trade is left with a remainder below Hyperliquid's $10 minimum, Trad closes it with a reduce-only order for exactly that amount.
A close that leaves such a remainder now completes instead of waiting for protection that cannot be placed.
Only stop or take-profit orders larger than the whole position are cancelled when they cannot be resized.

details.title: Dust is closed automatically
items: Happens only when the leftover is the entire exchange position on that side, so the close cannot touch other exposure.
Sent once per trade; if the exchange refuses it, the small remainder stays visible on the trade.

details.title: Closes finish with sub-minimum remainders
items: A close no longer stays in 'settling protection' when the remaining protection is too small for the exchange.
A stop or take-profit that still fits inside the position is left alone when it cannot be resized.

summary: Fast partial closes and slow exchange replies no longer lock the whole account, protection edits only count as done once the exchange shows them, and live prices recover after a feed restart.
fixes: A problem with one trade's protection no longer stops every other trade on the account.
Moving a stop or take-profit is only marked done once the exchange shows the new price; an edit that did not reach the exchange is sent again.
Edits you make to Trad's orders directly on the exchange are kept rather than undone.
When a remainder is too small for the exchange minimum, the larger stop or take-profit is cancelled instead of being left on the position.
Take-profit levels now cover the whole filled size, without leaving a tiny leftover.
Live prices and P&L return on their own after the market feed restarts.

details.title: Fewer account lockups
items: Exchange replies that arrive out of order during fast partial closes no longer put the account into recovery.
Exchange lookups always finish, and a lookup that cannot be completed is retried instead of waiting for a restart.
If one protection cannot be confirmed, only that trade waits for the exchange; other trades continue.

details.title: Protection matches the exchange
items: Trad reads the real trigger and limit prices from the exchange instead of assuming its request was applied.
A stop or take-profit edit that never reached the exchange is sent again automatically.
Price edits made directly on the exchange to a Trad order become the plan, so later size changes keep them.

details.title: Small remainders
items: Take-profit levels round together so the last level takes the remainder of the fill.
A stop or take-profit that would be larger than a sub-minimum remainder is cancelled; the small remainder stays visible on the trade.

details.title: Market feed recovery
items: A temporary market-feed interruption keeps the price subscription open, and the next real price restores live P&L.
Open browser tabs need a reload after this update.

summary: Prevents unnecessary protection and Chase reconciliation failures, and keeps last-trade P&L visible when a connected market is quiet.
minor: Live P&L shows the age of the last trade when no new trade has arrived for 15 seconds.
fixes: Protection waiting for the exchange minimum size no longer fails reconciliation when an unchanged position is checked again.
Chase quantity changes already covered by an in-flight modification no longer trigger an unnecessary reconciliation warning.
A missing order during an audit without a recovery operation is retried against current order history instead of being treated as a fatal query failure.
Quiet markets retain last-trade P&L, while exchange-feed interruptions are reported to the browser as unavailable.

details.title: Protection resumes when its target changes
items: Repeated checks of an unchanged position no longer reuse a finished protection operation as pending work.
Additional entry fills that change the protection target can prepare new work, while protection below the exchange minimum remains deferred.

details.title: Chase modification and recovery handling
items: Recognize when an unresolved modification already represents the desired quantity and continue waiting for its outcome.
Retry an audit that cannot find its captured order identity using the latest recorded order history. Uncertain exchange outcomes still require confirmation.

details.title: Market-feed failures reach the trade card
items: Preserve exchange-feed interruption signals through the market stream so the browser can distinguish a disconnected feed from a market with no new trades.
Keep recovered price windows consistent after connection-status events and associate ongoing feed errors with the active subscription.

details.title: Last-trade age stays visible
items: Keep live P&L based on the last traded price during quiet periods and display the trade's age after 15 seconds.
An explicit feed failure still makes live P&L unavailable. Final realized P&L and exchange stop-trigger settings are unchanged.

summary: Take-profit fills now spend their original allocation instead of replenishing from the remaining position.
fixes: A filled take-profit no longer refills itself or shrinks a surviving take-profit simply because the position became smaller.
New entry fills earn only their own take-profit allocation while the stop continues to cover the remaining position.
Protection edits and restarts retain spent allocations and account for late fills from replaced orders.

details.title: Take-profit allocations follow acquired units
items: Each acquired entry unit earns its configured take-profit distribution once. A take-profit execution spends only that level's allocation.
Chase and trailing entry continue under their existing entry instructions; only additional entry fills can earn new take-profit allocation.
Manual reductions proportionally reduce outstanding take-profit allocations, and price-only edits preserve allocation history.
Existing trades retain their surviving take-profit targets when upgraded. Reconciliation warnings remain visible when exchange evidence is incomplete.

summary: Restores editing of Chase stops and take profits whose existing allocations were stored in the engine's pro-rata format.
fixes: Existing Chase protection now loads into the editor instead of being incorrectly reported as an invalid allocation.
A single stop or take-profit price edit retains the other live protection legs and their exact existing allocations.

details.title: Edit existing Chase protection
items: Read the engine's nested pro-rata take-profit allocation without changing the saved plan or current exchange orders when opening the editor.
Route a one-price edit through the focused protection amendment, preserving unchanged stop and take-profit terms.
No backend or database change is required; opening the editor does not submit an order change.

summary: Restores live prices for non-default markets and explains why a taken-over trade can lack final P&L.
minor: Taken-over trade cards explain when final P&L cannot be calculated because complete attributed exit fills are absent.
fixes: Bounded market windows now report the first returned sequence, restoring live-price subscriptions for markets with more than one window of retained trades.
Taken-over historical trades no longer maintain unnecessary live-price subscriptions or show a misleading Live net label.

details.title: Live-price window continuity
items: Align the window's oldest sequence with its first returned sample when the requested limit truncates retained history.
Keep last-trade price as Trad's selected live P&L source; this release does not change exchange-native stop triggers or trade accounting.

details.title: Historical takeover clarity
items: Explain that Trad cannot show final net P&L without complete fills attributed to the trade after Take Over.
Stop subscribing taken-over cards to the live market feed and label their result as historical rather than live.

summary: Reduces idle Hyperliquid traffic, coordinates one outbound-IP request budget, makes account readiness explicit, and diagnoses missing live P&L inputs.
major: Gateway and node now reserve Hyperliquid REST weight through one durable per-egress-IP budget, including shared cooldown after a rate-limit response.
Idle account preflight runs less often while retaining bounded freshness before new exposure and preserving risk-reducing actions.
The single-node deployment visibly refuses Hyperliquid accounts beyond its monitored private-stream capacity instead of starting an unmonitored owner.
minor: Account controls explain setup and reconciliation readiness before opening actions become available; close and cancel paths remain available.
Live P&L distinguishes an initial price wait, stale market evidence, market-feed failure, and incomplete financial evidence.
Bounded market-stream telemetry records state transitions and freshness categories without recording prices, P&L, wallet data, or raw exchange messages.
fixes: Timestamp-only agent and builder approval observations no longer restart an otherwise unchanged account owner.
Hyperliquid information endpoints use their documented request weights, and setup, reload, validation, approval, scheduled reads, and venue actions share the same budget.
P&L freshness now advances on a reactive clock, and closed trades no longer retain an unnecessary live-market subscription.

details.title: Shared Hyperliquid capacity
items: Coordinate Gateway and node request reservations through PostgreSQL using the deployment's stable egress key.
Keep maintenance, new-risk, and risk-reduction ceilings separate so background work cannot consume the final exit headroom.
Retain the five-minute evidence expiry while moving ordinary idle refresh to three minutes and failed refresh retry to 30 seconds.
Permit eight private accounts with one public market network, or seven total private accounts when two public networks are active.

details.title: Readiness and market diagnostics
items: Keep opening actions unavailable until both the browser projection and server reconciliation state are ready without blocking risk reduction.
Report subscribing, waiting, ready, stale, and typed error transitions at bounded cardinality.
Show whether live P&L lacks a first price, has an old price, lost its feed, or lacks complete fill and fee evidence.

summary: Tracks exact physical order replacements, improves existing protection edits and closed-trade accounting, and makes Chase closes quicker to use.
major: Physical order lineage now distinguishes a logical order from each venue order it has replaced, so cancel, modify, and outcome checks remain tied to the intended physical child.
Existing stops and take-profits can be amended as focused child moves while retaining the rest of the accepted protection plan.
Chase is the default managed-trade close mode, with its adverse boundary and expiry visible before a guarded one-tap close.
minor: Stop controls offer move-to-entry, server-calculated fee-aware breakeven, and an explicit price target.
Trade cards distinguish live gross and net results from final realized P&L and keep missing accounting evidence explicit.
Narrow-screen action dialogs, protection legs, and submit controls are easier to reach.
Preview rejection is separated from an accepted command, and account badges distinguish loading, resync, exchange checks, and a genuine sync block.
fixes: Closed managed-trade P&L now links native stop exits through the owning protection scope instead of treating the exit as absent.
A retained stop move no longer appends a second stop or silently replaces unrelated take-profit children.
Known browser-extension exceptions are no longer presented as Trad interface failures without app-origin evidence.
Legacy cancel-outcome queries recover their parent's exact physical target during old snapshot and event replay.
Historical event-only recovery understands the bounded reconciliation and protection-pointer shapes written by older builds without relaxing current-state validation.

details.title: Exact physical order identity
items: Retain predecessor and successor venue identities across replacements without confusing either with the logical order.
Bind modifications and cancellation checks to one physical target and reject evidence from a retired sibling as proof for a newer child.
Upgrade old cancel-query records from their parent's immutable target when restoring pre-0.10.12 data.

details.title: Focused protection and closing actions
items: Prefill the accepted protection ladder, preserve retained child identities, and change only the selected stop or take-profit.
Calculate fee-aware breakeven on the server from attributed fills instead of estimating it in the browser.
Keep a Chase close pending after an uncertain response until its exact command reaches a terminal projected outcome.

details.title: Trade presentation and recovery
items: Join native stop fills to their protection owner before computing final scoped P&L; show incomplete when essential fills or fee assets disagree.
Show temporary preview and account-recovery states without implying that a rejected preview placed an order.
Classify known injected-provider errors separately from verified app-origin failures.
Normalize only the exact legacy reconciliation waits and terminal protection pointers required to reconstruct older event streams; keep current payloads strict.

summary: Adds fee-aware risk sizing, smoother account-session handoff, safer manual takeover, and stronger physical-order recovery across managed workflows.
major: Risk-sized entries now reserve expected entry and stop-exit fees inside the user's accepted risk budget, then consume exact reported fees as fills arrive.
A live Chase recalculates its permitted remainder from current price, exact fills, and remaining fee-adjusted risk without exceeding the quantity accepted at placement.
Planned connection renewal keeps the current account session usable until its replacement is authenticated and authoritative.
Take Over now transfers management control immediately while exact cancellation of known Trad-owned exchange orders continues as visible cleanup.
minor: Trade details expose the pinned fee assumptions, actual fee consumption, remaining risk, and current permitted quantity without combining builder attribution twice.
Preview results are fenced to the exact draft revision so an older success or failure cannot change the current form.
Sanitized production-shaped event replay and deterministic lifecycle graph checks now gate the candidate locally.
Binance and Bybit account setup and engine placement are temporarily paused while their adapters, historical records, and compatibility paths remain available for future reactivation.
fixes: Fixed a rejected Hyperliquid native-modify successor failing to retry when its physical predecessor had partially filled.
Fixed late predecessor evidence or fee recalculation bypassing the fresh-book wait for a post-only Chase retry.
Fixed retired physical-order evidence completing work that targets a newer successor in Chase and native-protection lineages.
Fixed delayed native-protection successor evidence leaving a recovered protection scope permanently fenced.
Fixed Trailing Entry protection fills, unknown resizes, and delayed entry evidence stranding valid recovery work.
Fixed Take Over waiting on exchange cleanup before releasing management control or allowing stale prepared work to dispatch.
Fixed a partially filled Chase resuming its unfilled entry after its own stop had already closed the exposure.
Fixed an editing-time preview failure briefly replacing a newer valid preview or appearing as a persistent trade error.

details.title: Fee-aware risk authorization
items: Pin the venue fee policy used when the command is accepted so later configuration changes cannot rewrite an active trade's contract.
Reserve maker entry and conservative stop-exit costs for every candidate quantity, then replace modeled entry cost with exact exchange evidence as fills settle.
Keep the original accepted quantity as a hard cap even when rebates, favorable fills, or lower later prices would otherwise permit growth.
Apply the same shared calculation boundary to supported opening order plans while preserving each controller's existing dispatch authority.

details.title: Physical successor lifecycle
items: Treat logical order ownership, logical generations, physical venue children, and exact query targets as separate identities.
Retry a zero-fill rejected native successor for only the aggregate unfilled remainder, even when its predecessor contributed valid fills.
Require a fresh book before the next post-only attempt and prevent late fills, fee updates, or retired rejection evidence from reopening dispatch early.
Keep exact TP and SL successor cancellation independent from terminal evidence belonging to an older physical child.

details.title: Manual control transfer
items: Detach Trad management as soon as Take Over is durably accepted instead of making user control wait for exchange cleanup.
Continue canceling every known Trad-owned entry, close, TP, and SL child by exact physical identity without closing the position.
Prevent books, timers, retries, restarts, and delayed evidence from preparing new risk-changing work after control transfers.
Keep ambiguous cleanup visible without silently restoring Trad ownership or adopting unrelated venue orders.

details.title: Protection and entry recovery
items: Clear a retired-predecessor protection fence only after exact successor evidence proves complete current coverage.
Allow exact terminal protection evidence to confirm an install while preserving the physical child identity needed by later work.
Bind unknown native installs and resizes only to a unique matching successor instead of guessing from a predecessor.
Terminalize constructive Chase work as soon as its stop begins filling, including after restart from an older persisted state.
Keep delayed zero-fill entry evidence from demoting a completed Trailing Entry while still accepting genuine late fills.

details.title: Session and release qualification
items: Keep an established browser transport active while a planned lease renewal obtains a fresh ticket and authoritative account snapshot.
Distinguish an exchange outcome still being confirmed from a genuine unexplained reconciliation mismatch.
Replay sanitized historical account events through the current engine and compare exact state, client projection, and operator projection digests.
Enumerate cancellation, rejection, partial-fill, delayed-evidence, and restart schedules and require every modeled state to retain a path to settlement.

summary: Kept risk-sized Chases aligned with their live fill prices while repairing retired-order hydration and exact protection cleanup.
major: Risk-sized opening Chases now recalculate their permitted remainder from exact fills, the current candidate price, and the authoritative stop instead of retaining an oversized initial quantity.
A retired physical Hyperliquid order remains part of its durable logical lineage, allowing startup reconciliation to consume late fills without trapping the account in Sync Unavailable.
When a protected scope becomes flat, obsolete undispatched resizes are retired and Trad proceeds to cancel only the exact surviving TP or SL child.
minor: Managed-trade metrics now show requested price risk, filled risk, projected stop loss, permitted remainder, and any confirmed overage.
Existing Chases created before this release retain their original fixed-size behavior; no historical risk budget is guessed during upgrade.
Fee, funding, and stop-slippage allowances remain outside this release and are identified separately from the live price-risk calculation.
fixes: Fixed partial Chase fills failing to resize toward the configured price-risk budget as price moves.
Fixed a historical fill on a retired Hyperliquid OID repeatedly preventing one account from hydrating while other accounts remained available.
Fixed an early partial protection fill leaving an obsolete resize actionable after later fills reduced the same owned target to zero.
Fixed manually canceled obsolete protection from being recreated when terminal venue absence already proves cleanup complete.

details.title: Live Chase price-risk authorization
items: Consume risk from every exact fill price across the logical Chase's physical order generations.
Recalculate the permitted unfilled quantity at each fresh candidate price and authoritative stop, rounded through the instrument's executable bounds.
Never grow beyond the initially accepted quantity cap, and authorize no new exposure at or through the stop.
Retarget only writes proven not to have reached the venue; reconcile every uncertain physical generation before creating a successor.

details.title: Retired physical-order recovery
items: Preserve every recorded Hyperliquid OID in its logical order lineage while keeping the active OID distinct for exact current-order queries.
Require an order-status response to match the exact OID requested without mistaking an older owned generation for a foreign order.
Apply late stop fills once, retire superseded undispatched resizes, and cancel only the exact remaining physical sibling.
Accept exact terminal absence after a user's manual cancel without reinstalling the obsolete TP or SL.

details.title: Lifecycle qualification
items: Replay production-sized Chase fills, retired OIDs, restarts, duplicates, late responses, cancellations, and retry-budget exhaustion.
Verify event replay and snapshot restore reproduce the same accounting, target quantity, operation lineage, and terminal state.
Rehearse the candidate on isolated production database copies with exchange effects disabled and zero claimed actions.
Keep unrelated accounts and valid protection orders unchanged while the affected account returns to active service.

summary: Recovered retired overlapping close fills as exact external reductions so authoritative startup can converge without hiding the resulting position.
major: An old close fill beyond its exact scope capacity is now preserved as an external reduction from that source order, never borrowed from another managed trade.
Fresh venue position evidence confirms the outside exposure and allows account activation instead of a repeating Sync Unavailable recovery cycle.
The recovery performs no automatic close or ownership claim; the resulting venue position remains explicitly outside every managed trade.
minor: The production-shaped generated campaign now requires successful activation semantics as well as replay-safe accounting conservation.
Expected post-only Chase races remain fresh-book paced and unbounded by the separate three-hard-rejection safety limit.
Forward lineage fencing and exact TP/SL cancellation identity from 0.10.7 remain unchanged.
fixes: Fixed known historic overfill recovery remaining trapped in startup because an otherwise authoritative position retained an unallocated-fill blocker.
Fixed a recovered account staying Sync Unavailable even after fresh venue evidence proved its exact external position.
Kept the retired order's excess quantity durable without weakening startup checks for genuinely unknown or ambiguous fills.

details.title: Exact externalization boundary
items: Apply a late reduction only up to the quantity its referenced exposure scope still owns.
Represent every excess unit as ReduceExternal with the same position side and source-order event.
Require authoritative venue position evidence to establish the resulting outside long or short quantity.
Leave unrelated unallocated fills and startup blockers strict; only this proven retired-reduction shape converges automatically.

details.title: Activation-loop rehearsal
items: Reproduced the production startup loop on a fresh read-only database copy with exchange effects disabled.
Verified the accounting repair before changing activation behavior, then rejected the intermediate release because it still left Sync Unavailable.
Require the final candidate to activate from the untouched production history while exposing the 6.61375 BTC position as external.
Never close, cancel, resize, or otherwise mutate the venue position during local rehearsal.

details.title: Generated recovery schedules
items: Permute two through nine overlapping reductions, partial fills, duplicate evidence, and arbitrary completion order.
Restart through event replay and snapshots between generated transitions.
Assert that owned exposure saturates at zero, excess never moves to another scope, and the authoritative residual is external.
Run the target in bounded CI and separate nightly and weekly campaigns.

summary: Recovered historic overlapping Chase closes without hiding their resulting external exposure or locking account hydration.
major: Historic close fills that exceed a trade's remaining owned quantity now preserve the excess as explicit unallocated exposure instead of preventing account startup.
The account converges to Reconciliation Required with the venue-observed position visible; Trad never silently claims, closes, or discards the excess.
Added deterministic production-number replay and generated schedules for overlapping reductions, late fills, duplicates, partials, and restarts.
minor: The 0.10.7 forward lineage fix remains intact: a post-only physical generation cannot terminate its parent Chase or release close ownership.
Generated recovery schedules assert accounting conservation across event replay and snapshot restore.
The recovery path performs no automatic financial action and leaves operator or customer resolution explicit.
fixes: Fixed an already-persisted overlapping close fill repeatedly failing owner hydration with reduction exceeds exposure scope.
Fixed excess historic reduction being represented only as a startup error instead of durable unallocated exposure.
Kept late physical-generation evidence bounded to its exact order while the logical Chase remains the lifecycle authority.

details.title: Backward-safe exposure recovery
items: Cap each historic owned-reduction effect at the quantity its exact exposure scope still owns.
Record every excess unit against its source order as unallocated fill rather than borrowing ownership from another trade.
Hydrate successfully into explicit reconciliation state with external venue exposure still visible and unchanged.
Preserve the normalized result in durable events so replay and snapshot restore cannot reinterpret it.

details.title: Production incident replay
items: Replay the 13.22751 BTC entry, 6.61375 BTC half-close, overlapping close-all, and retired half-close fill in their observed order.
Require owned exposure to reach exactly zero while the resulting 6.61375 BTC short remains external and requires reconciliation.
Verify the same result after duplicate evidence, event replay, and snapshot restoration instead of a repeating hydration failure.

details.title: Sustained overlap campaign
items: Generate two through nine historic reductions with arbitrary fill ordering and partial completion.
Inject duplicate fills and event or snapshot restarts between every meaningful transition.
Cross through flat in the fake Hyperliquid model and require exact conservation of owned, external, and unallocated quantities.
Run bounded CI plus longer nightly and weekly shards independently from routine product tests.

summary: Kept post-only Chase races inside their owning trade and close lineage without unlocking overlapping actions.
major: Post-only submit and native-modify races now wait for fresh market evidence without consuming the Chase hard-failure budget.
A live close Chase retains exclusive ownership of its exposure scope across every physical order generation, duplicate, late predecessor event, and restart.
Added a dedicated generated Chase lineage campaign covering repeated submit and modify races, snapshot and event replay, and overlapping close attempts.
minor: Close controls now distinguish exchange confirmation from a stable reconciliation blocker and explain which active close owns the trade.
Hyperliquid capacity guidance remains advisory so stale balance evidence never becomes a hard client-side trading gate.
Release qualification includes deterministic incident replays plus bounded CI, nightly, and sustained fuzz shards.
fixes: Fixed Hyperliquid badAloPxRejected evidence dropping a zero-fill Chase instead of repricing from the next book update.
Fixed one rejected physical close generation falsely failing its parent and allowing another close to cross the account through flat.
Fixed stale predecessor cancellation evidence discharging work intended for the newest TP or SL successor.

details.title: One Chase, many physical generations
items: Treat each venue CLOID and OID as one physical attempt while the Chase and parent close remain the lifecycle authorities.
Require a later fresh book before exactly one retry can be prepared, with one operation in flight and normal cancel, boundary, and deadline controls intact.
Keep genuine hard native-modify failures separately bounded while expected post-only races remain normal Chase churn.
Preserve backward replay compatibility by decoding older untyped rejection events conservatively as hard unclassified failures.

details.title: Close ownership and exact cancellation
items: Follow the whole close Chase lifecycle instead of terminalizing the parent from one rejected physical generation.
Defensively reserve an exposure scope whenever its parent, Chase, or referenced order still contains live work.
Require exact remote-order identity before a predecessor cancellation or query can resolve a current normal or protection successor.
Explain active close ownership and exchange-confirmation progress without flashing a stable reconciliation error for ordinary latency.

details.title: Generated incident qualification
items: Generate one through thirty-two consecutive submit or native-modify races per schedule.
Inject duplicate responses, late generation-one evidence, event replay, snapshot restore, and competing partial or full closes.
Require the parent to remain Closing, reject every overlap, retain zero hard-failure count for expected races, and eventually fill exactly once.
Run the target in bounded CI and separate longer nightly and weekly campaigns so ordinary tests remain fast.

summary: Added privacy-bounded first-party incident timelines for user intent, blockers, transport, and durable command correlation.
major: Financial actions now carry one attempt identity across form, preview, Gateway request, durable command acceptance, and projected terminal outcome.
Reconciliation-blocked close and protection controls explain the exact stable blocker instead of silently swallowing attempted user actions.
Administrators can query an audited chronological incident timeline by user, account, trade, session, attempt, request, or command identity.
minor: Added bounded memory-only collection for meaningful navigation, field interaction, account authority changes, connection state, projection gaps, and support references.
Added an explicit server-side cohort allowlist so internal rollout can be enforced before any broader collection decision.
Added a separate short-timeout telemetry pool, fixed event and byte budgets, account ownership checks, retention batches, and health counters.
fixes: Telemetry failures, malformed events, rate limits, queue overflow, storage outage, and pool contention now drop observations without entering financial control flow.
Late predecessor evidence and sequence gaps remain visible without being reordered into invented certainty, while one attempt cannot link to two durable commands.
Collection and retention remain disabled by default; rollback can stop collection independently without changing trading binaries or deleting audit history.

details.title: Correlated incident timelines
items: Follow one user attempt from modal open or blocked control through preview, request, response, durable command, and terminal projection evidence.
Distinguish browser interaction, browser-observed transport, and browser-observed durable identifiers while keeping engine and exchange records authoritative.
Record Sync Unavailable, reconciliation banners, account selection, diagnostics, Settings navigation, agent changes, retries, and abandonment as stable typed events.
Audit every administrative timeline lookup and require a bounded incident selector.

details.title: Non-interference and privacy
items: Use an asynchronous collector with a bounded memory-only queue, fixed retry count, maximum age, and no local storage.
Reject free text, unknown properties, secrets, raw request bodies, oversized values, invalid identities, clock skew, and accounts not owned by the authenticated user.
Keep telemetry in additive tables and a separately bounded pool with no foreign keys or transaction dependency from financial state.
Drop open on disabled collection, malformed input, storage failure, rate limiting, and pool exhaustion.

details.title: Disabled-first rollout
items: Ship the release with collection and retention off unless explicitly configured.
Allow only an explicit internal UUID cohort before any bounded or general rollout.
Expose accepted, dropped, invalid, duplicate, throttled, storage-failure, and sequence-gap health counters.
Require retention, notice, export/deletion, access, volume, and production-clone gates before broad enablement.

summary: Completed the multi-venue state-machine campaign and hardened account removal against owner and storage races.
major: Added maintained generated campaigns for order lineage, protection, external venue activity, balances, configuration, account lifecycle, ownership, durability, projections, isolation, and three venue profiles.
Account removal quarantine now survives lease expiry, preventing another owner from reacquiring an account after credentials were erased but before assignment retirement completed.
Configuration and removal schedules now continuously exercise stale credentials, disable and re-enable, committed effects, owner epochs, and retry boundaries without exchange access.
minor: Added dedicated bounded fuzz targets and seed corpora for account configuration and removal.
Kept nightly and weekly campaigns isolated, reproducible, and subject to corpus, artifact, target, memory, and time budgets.
fixes: Fixed local-only account removal becoming non-resumable when credential deletion failed after the durable quarantine was installed.
Fixed an expired quarantined assignment being eligible for owner reacquisition before destructive account removal retired it.
Required stale owners to remain fenced after an account is removed and recreated with a fresh owner epoch.

details.title: Multi-venue state-machine campaign
items: Run shared semantic order and evidence histories through Hyperliquid, Binance, and Bybit capability profiles.
Compose user actions, direct venue activity, response timing, snapshots, balance changes, credential revisions, owner transfer, durable retry, and replay.
Require every generated history to converge, wait on named bounded evidence, or enter an explicit stable blocker instead of looping invisibly.
Keep deterministic regressions in routine tests and long coverage-guided runs in isolated bounded targets.

details.title: Account removal fencing
items: Resume only a quarantine created by the explicit unverified-removal workflow; an unrelated operator quarantine remains ineligible.
Keep credential-erasure quarantine authoritative even after its lease deadline passes.
Block removal while committed or claimed exchange effects exist and retire only the exact fenced lease.
Require recreation to acquire a fresh owner epoch that stale cleanup cannot mutate.

details.title: Bounded campaign operations
items: Add source-controlled CI, nightly, and weekly shards for configuration and account removal.
Pin the fuzz toolchain and enforce build, corpus, artifact, report, file-count, and execution-time limits.
Run runtime targets only with in-memory journals and the synthetic Bifake executor, with no credential or real-exchange path.

summary: Restored account hydration and TP/SL convergence after terminal dust and rapid partial-close races.
major: Terminal partial fills now settle their actual owned quantity without leaving impossible protection lineage behind.
Rapid partial-close fill bursts now leave reconciliation only after every newest TP and SL successor exactly matches the remaining owned quantity.
Successor and cancellation evidence remains bound to the exact physical exchange order it proves.
minor: Expanded deterministic exchange simulation, replay, snapshot, and multi-venue conformance coverage.
Recorded the broader versioned-lineage timing class for the dedicated fuzz campaign following this hotfix.
fixes: Fixed accounts becoming Sync unavailable after a minimum-notional terminal partial left a canceled protection scope with pending lineage.
Fixed Close ⅓ leaving an otherwise exact TP/SL pair permanently reconciliation-required after intermediate successors briefly exceeded the final target.
Fixed minimum-notional preparation deferrals retaining actionable operations that could never reach the exchange.

details.title: Exact successor convergence
items: Keep the overcoverage fence while any child remains oversized, failed, or has pending predecessor/successor work.
Clear only the known transient overcoverage reason after every physical child is exact and pending-free.
Let ordinary coverage derivation move the controller to Tracking, Flat, or Canceled without weakening unrelated reconciliation failures.
Replay the production two-child, thirteen-fill ordering and require identical event replay and snapshot restoration.

details.title: Terminal dust lifecycle
items: Account for the quantity actually filled when an entry becomes terminal below its requested quantity.
Supersede minimum-notional protection work before dispatch and clear its pending child link.
Allow owner recovery to hydrate the resulting effect-free account instead of repeating the same reconciliation failure.

details.title: Deferred fuzz campaign seed
items: Register rapid target-version changes, in-flight intermediate successors, and prepared-query stream resolution as a dedicated protection schedule.
Require convergence only from exact newest-child evidence, with unrelated safety fences remaining sticky.
Keep the long-running campaign expansion separate from this urgent deterministic patch and deployment qualification.

summary: Hardened TP/SL cancellation against predecessor-successor races and expanded generated reconciliation-liveness coverage.
major: Protection cancels now require terminal evidence for the exact physical exchange order they target, preventing retired predecessors from discharging live-successor cancels.
NativeProtection, StopGuard, and normal order modify/cancel flows now have generated timing and recovery tests with explicit convergence oracles.
Exact exchange absence is now durable, monotonic, replayable, and wakes dependent close workflows.
minor: Managed trades expose a compact copy control for their stable root command ID to make incident reports unambiguous.
Removed user-triggered reconciliation controls while retaining backend-owned reconciliation and recovery.
Reduced routine Rust test artifact size while retaining source-level backtraces and an on-demand full-debug profile.
fixes: Fixed Chase closes leaving resized TP and SL successors live after predecessor cancellation events arrived.
Fixed wrong-child and stale-predecessor query evidence becoming terminal instead of retrying or entering a healable reconciliation state.
Fixed exact-absence convergence being lost across journal replay or failing to refresh close settlement.

details.title: Exact physical-order cancellation
items: Require direct TP/SL cancellation observations, cancellation queries, and snapshot absence to prove the exact target remote order terminal.
Require known resize/install successor acknowledgements to be confirmed by that successor identity.
Prevent terminal predecessor evidence from proving an unknown normal-order modify successor terminal.
Reject actionable NativeProtection links to terminal operations except an explicitly failed reconciliation query retained as a healing sentinel.

details.title: Generated reconciliation liveness
items: Vary close and acknowledgement timing, missing responses, duplicate observations, wrong predecessor or child evidence, snapshots, recovery pulses, retry exhaustion, and eventual exact venue evidence.

Require every generated case to clear actionable mutations, terminalize or prove absent every relevant physical child, converge the logical workflow, validate invariants, and restore identically from durable state.
Exercise NativeProtection resize-to-close, multi-child StopGuard close, and normal order modify-to-cancel lineages on every ordinary Engine suite run.

details.title: Restart and recovery correctness
items: Record authoritative exact absence as a dedicated domain event and reconstruct it during journal replay.
Normalize absence revision against retained venue evidence so query timestamps cannot regress protection inventory.
Wake close settlement whenever exact absence changes protection state and allow later exact inventory to heal bounded reconciliation exhaustion.

details.title: Safer operational surface
items: Keep reconciliation automatic and backend-owned instead of exposing a browser action that appears to repair state manually.
Expose stable trade identity beside each managed trade for faster support correlation.
Keep full debugger information available through an explicit test-debug profile without embedding it into every routine test executable.

summary: Restored reliable account authorization, reconciliation readiness, and account removal after agent rotation or external venue activity.
major: Account configuration changes now recover the affected owner when its private stream is not yet active instead of deadlocking revision reload.
External exchange orders retain authoritative economic scope across private-stream updates, preventing perpetual reconciliation churn.
Added an explicit Remove from Trad only path that preserves history and leaves venue state untouched.
minor: Account deletion now distinguishes verified exchange cleanup from deliberate local detachment.
Agent replacement recovery is bounded to the affected account owner and keeps new risk blocked until the latest configuration starts cleanly.
fixes: Fixed accounts remaining stuck in reconciling after a Trad-owned Hyperliquid agent was replaced or revoked.
Fixed repeated external-order observations making an otherwise scoped account appear unready.
Fixed deletion retries piling up behind a reconciliation refresh that could never become ready.

details.title: Agent-rotation recovery
items: Detect configuration reloads that cannot quiesce because the current private stream is unavailable, already pending, or timed out.
Fence and stop only the affected owner, install the latest prepared account configuration, and restart hydration under the current assignment lease.
Subscribe to owner lifecycle events before stopping so a fast terminal event cannot be missed.
Bound the restart barrier and roll back partially installed owner resources when restart fails.
Keep new exposure blocked throughout recovery and unlock it only after normal preflight and stream activation complete.
Treat direct venue-side deletion of Trad's agent as a recoverable authorization change: the user must approve the replacement in Trad, but other accounts remain available.

details.title: Stable reconciliation readiness
items: Preserve authoritative symbol, side, quantity, and price scope when a system-external order receives a subsequent private-stream observation.
Prevent private updates from turning a scoped external order back into an unscoped order that blocks account readiness.
Stop the five-second restore-and-erase loop that continually scheduled new reconciliation refreshes.
Retain conservative readiness checks for genuinely unknown external orders rather than weakening reconciliation policy.
Cover the production sequence with a regression that classifies an authoritative external order, applies a live update, and proves readiness remains stable.

details.title: Two explicit account-removal modes
items: Keep Check and delete as the verified path that reconciles exchange state before removing an account.
Add Remove from Trad only as an explicitly confirmed path for an effect-free account when exchange verification is unavailable or unwanted.
Stop the local account owner, fence its exact lease, erase stored exchange credentials, and retire its assignment without sending cancel, close, or reconciliation effects to the venue.
Retain immutable commands, trades, fills, and audit history after local detachment.
Block local-only removal while committed or claimed exchange effects remain, avoiding ambiguous in-flight delivery.
Explain in both confirmation steps that venue positions and orders remain untouched and unmanaged after detachment.

details.title: Qualification included in this hotfix
items: Run the complete backend workspace test suite and production unwrap lint.
Exercise configuration replacement before private-stream activation with a deterministic never-connecting connector.
Exercise active effect-free account detachment and reject detachment when effects or draining ownership are present.
Build and type-check the complete frontend, including release-specific test and production social previews.
Restore exact test and production database clones locally and start the candidate with exchange effects disabled before deployment.

summary: Scoped trade accounting, safer Chase protection, precise fee administration, and a denser trading workflow.
major: Added trade-scoped live PnL, risk, and fee accounting that stays separate from external Hyperliquid exposure.
Reworked Chase protection around immediate stop growth, proportional take-profit growth, and explicit confirmed coverage.
Added administrator-controlled global, user, and account all-in fee policy with immutable trade snapshots and revenue reporting.
minor: Duplicate Trade now restores the original authored sizing, Chase, protection, and execution settings.
Builder-approval failures now explain the required action and link directly to account authorization.
Added direction-aware stop-loss presets and automatic Hyperliquid price normalization.
Condensed trade economics, risk, fees, creation time, and close actions into denser trade rows.
Added a versioned Patch Notes area with development-only draft previews.
fixes: Fixed the BTC rapid-fill race that compared an older protection query with a newer desired quantity.
Fixed TAO take-profit dust rejection by deferring children below the venue minimum until they become executable.
Fixed protection replacement lineage so a retired predecessor is not reported as unexplained missing coverage.
Fixed Take Over trades remaining in Active after Trad management had been detached.
Fixed fee reports that lost accepted policy snapshots or rejected filtered account pagination.
Fixed trade metric truncation, unnecessary close confirmations, and several builder-remediation contrast failures.

details.title: Trade-scoped economics and risk
items: Compute each managed trade's entry basis from fills allocated to that durable exposure scope instead of borrowing Hyperliquid's one-way net-position cost basis.
Keep externally created same-symbol exposure out of a Trad trade's realized and unrealized PnL.
Show scoped Live PnL beside Realized net on the top-level trade row, using the latest accepted Trad market sample and an explicit unavailable or stale state.
Retain exact per-fill realized PnL and fee evidence inside History and Execution without inventing device-level PnL ownership.
Separate requested Risk budget, accepted Initial planned loss to stop, and Current risk to stop.
Persist the accepted sizing mode, requested risk, decision price, stop, normalized quantity, instrument rules, and fee assumptions needed to reproduce risk after restart.
Keep initial risk immutable while fills, partial closes, and protection amendments update only current remaining risk.
Display actual exchange fees, Trad builder fees, pinned all-in target, and policy source on each managed trade.

details.title: Chase protection controller
items: Grow the full stop immediately whenever accepted entry fills increase managed exposure.
